panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Human renal-biopsy H&E image showing foamy glomerular endothelial cells, corresponding to the configured glomerular foam-cell/lipidosis finding in an article specifically about familial LCAT deficiency. B: PAS-stained renal glomerulus demonstrating mesangial proliferation, supporting mesangial expansion in familial LCAT deficiency-associated nephropathy. C: Human renal-biopsy PASM image with captioned basement-membrane vacuolization and a double-track sign in a case diagnosed as familial LCAT deficiency; these findings are not represented in the allowed vocabulary. D: Masson-stained human renal biopsy from the familial LCAT deficiency case, captioned as negative for immune deposits. The characteristic feature is not in the supplied vocabulary. E: Oil red O-stained renal biopsy demonstrates glomerular lipid deposition, directly supporting glomerular lipidosis in familial LCAT deficiency. F: Oil red O-stained renal tissue shows...

panels.figure_caption: Light microscopy findings on renal biopsy. (A) H&E staining: dilated capillary loops with vacuolar thrombus-like material (black arrows) and foamy endothelial cells (white arrows). (B) PAS staining: mesangial proliferation (black arrows) and basement membrane thickening (white arrows). (C) PASM staining: vacuolar areas in basement membrane (white arrows) with double-track sign (black arrows). (D) Masson’s stain: negative for immune deposits. (E,F) Oil red O stain: positive lipid droplets in glomeruli and tubular cells (black arrows). ×400.
in_text_mentions: Given the patient’s history of corneal opacity since childhood (Figure 2), lipid abnormalities with a marked reduction in HDL-C, and nephrotic syndrome, hereditary lipoprotein metabolic disorders, particularly LCAT deficiency-related nephropathy, were strongly suspected. To clarify the pathological nature of the renal involvement, a renal biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed glomerular lipid deposition, confirming the diagnosis of LCAT deficiency-related renal damage (Figures 3–5).
